title: Search across every file
summary: Use the Search view to find a word in the whole folder and open a match.

steps.say: Check that a folder is open. The Explorer on the left should list files. Say done when it does.
hints: If the Explorer says no folder is open, do the lesson Open a project folder first.
Press Control Shift E to show the Explorer.
steps.why: Search looks through the open folder, so it needs one.

steps.say: Press Control Shift F to open Search in the side bar.

checks.prompt: Is the Search view open in the left side bar with an empty search box?

hints: Search is the magnifying glass icon, second in the Activity Bar at the far left.
Or open the View menu and choose Search.
steps.why: The Search view finds text in every file at once, not only the open one.

steps.say: Type a word that appears in your files, such as the name of a function or a heading.

checks.prompt: Does the Search view list results grouped under file names?

hints: Results appear as you type, grouped by file.
The small buttons in the box turn on match case, whole word and regular expressions.
steps.why: Seeing every match helps you understand where something is used.

steps.say: Click one of the result lines to jump to it in the editor.

checks.prompt: Is a file open in the editor with the searched word highlighted?

hints: Each indented line under a file name is one match.
Press F4 to jump to the next match without the mouse.
steps.why: Results link straight to the exact line, which saves scrolling.

steps.say: Press Control Shift E to go back to the Explorer.

checks.prompt: Does the left side bar show the Explorer file tree again?

hints: Explorer is the top icon in the Activity Bar.
Clicking the active Activity Bar icon again hides the side bar.
steps.why: Switching side bar views by keyboard keeps your hands off the mouse.
